 Description du poste 
 Services SFT recherche activement un(e) Infirmier(ère) d'expérience en soins périnatals pour combler un mandat temporaire à temps complet au département d' Obstétrique de l'Hôpital de Chandler (CISSS de la Gaspésie) .
 Ce mandat de trois mois est une opportunité idéale pour une infirmière spécialisée souhaitant mettre son expertise au profit des futures mamans et des nouveau-nés de la région, tout en bénéficiant des excellentes conditions de la grille des régions éloignées.
 Détails du mandat : 
 Numéro de référence : R#1844
 Période : Du 1er novembre au 1er février 2027 
 Statut : Temps complet ( 75 heures par 2 semaines )
 Horaire : Horaire atypique avec rotation sur les quarts de Jour / Soir / Nuit 
 Responsabilités 
 Au sein de l'unité d'obstétrique, vos principales fonctions engloberont la prise en charge complète du couple mère-enfant :
 Assurer le suivi et la surveillance clinique rigoureuse des patientes en phase d' ante-partum .
 Prendre en charge le travail et assister activement le médecin lors de l' accouchement .
 Dispenser les soins post-opératoires et le suivi de récupération immédiate en post-partum pour la mère et le nouveau-né.
 Évaluer l'état de santé du nouveau-né à la naissance et effectuer les manœuvres de stabilisation si nécessaire.
 Assurer les enseignements cliniques essentiels aux nouveaux parents (allaitement, soins postnataux).
 Exigences 
 Pour que votre dossier de candidature soit soumis au CISSS, vous devez nous fournir les documents démontrant les critères obligatoires suivants :
 Expérience : Détenir un minimum de 2 ans d'expérience récente combinée en ante-partum, salle d'accouchement et post-partum.
 Certification obligatoire : Détenir la certification NRP (Neonatal Resuscitation Program / Réanimation néonatale) à jour .
 Ordre professionnel : Être membre en règle de l' OIIQ (permis d'exercice valide).
 Urgences : Certification RCR à jour .
 Mobilité : Permis de conduire valide.
 Avantages et conditions: 
 Rémunération supérieure et primes associées aux spécialités fermées (Obstétrique).
 Per diem quotidien octroyé pour toute la durée de votre assignation.
 Prise en charge logistique : Hébergement fourni et remboursement de vos frais de déplacement par l'établissement.
 Accompagnement rigoureux, fiable et humain par l'équipe de Services SFT.
 Intéressé(e) ? 
 Envoyez votre CV à jour à :
 info.sft@sftechniques.com 
 Vous pouvez également nous contacter au (438) 946-6340 .
 Notre équipe se fera un plaisir de répondre à toutes vos questions.

 The Workday Solutions Delivery Manager is accountable end to end for Workday solution delivery, resource management, and operational performance within the HCM Technology portfolio. The role owns execution across Program Increment (PI) delivery, Workday enhancements, AMS oversight, production support, resource capacity and allocation, continuous improvement, and small-to-medium Workday projects.  
 As the primary technology delivery partner for Workday stakeholders, this leader is accountable not only for individual deliverables but also for making sure the right resources and skills are applied to the highest-priority work at the right time. The role combines solution ownership, delivery leadership, service management, and resource management, and remains accountable for outcomes whether work is performed by internal resources or strategic delivery partners.   
 This is an individual-contributor role with no direct reports. The Workday Solutions Delivery Manager leads through influence, clear plans, transparent reporting, and agreed accountability with internal teams, HCM Solution Managers, and delivery partners.  
 Key Responsibilities   
 PI Planning & Delivery   
 Own execution of Workday PI commitments within the assigned solution portfolio.   
 Translate approved business priorities into executable delivery plans and resource requirements.   
 Maintain the Workday delivery backlog so work is refined, estimated, prioritized, and sequenced.   
 Establish achievable PI commitments based on priority, technical dependencies, and available capacity and capability; do not accept commitments without a realistic assessment of both.   
 Coordinate functional, technical, integration, security, testing, and vendor resources required for delivery.   
 Monitor execution against PI commitments and proactively address schedule, scope, dependency, capacity, or quality issues.   
 Provide accurate delivery forecasts and regular reporting on committed versus completed scope, risks, trade-offs, and decisions required.   
 Resource Management, Capacity Planning & Allocation 
This is a core accountability of the role, not an administrative responsibility. The role directs the allocation of Workday delivery capacity without direct people-management responsibility.   
 Own resource planning and allocation across Workday PI delivery, AMS, enhancements, technical debt, and small projects.   
 Maintain an integrated view of Workday demand, available capacity, required skills, committed resources, utilization, and upcoming demand.   
 Allocate internal and partner resources based on business priorities, delivery commitments, operational risk, and required technical and functional skills, in coordination with resource owners.   
 Balance capacity between planned PI delivery and BAU and production-support requirements.   
 Identify capacity constraints, skill gaps, and resource conflicts before they affect delivery commitments; recommend prioritization, sequencing, scope adjustment, or incremental capacity when demand exceeds available resources.   
 Partner with vendors so appropriate functional and technical capabilities are assigned to Workday technical deliverable, and challenge vendor staffing that does not meet agreed skill, quality, or performance expectations.   
 Manage transitions, onboarding, knowledge transfer, and continuity for resources supporting the Workday service.   
 Reduce dependency on individual resources through documentation, cross-training, and succession coverage.   
 Provide resource and capacity forecasts as inputs to HCM portfolio and financial planning, and keep assignments aligned with funded capacity and approved portfolio priorities.   
 Escalate structural capacity or capability gaps with clear recommendations and business impact.   
 Workday AMS & Production Service Ownership   
 Own day-to-day oversight of Workday AMS within the assigned portfolio.   
 Ensure incidents, service requests, defects, and problems are prioritized, assigned, and resolved effectively.   
 Manage ticket backlog, aging, SLA performance, recurring issues, and production risk.   
 Ensure ServiceNow accurately reflects issue status, accountability, and resolution.   
 Require root-cause analysis for significant or recurring incidents, and track corrective actions that address underlying causes through completion.   
 Monitor vendor resource performance, technical and functional quality, continuity, and knowledge coverage.   
 Hold AMS providers accountable for proactive support and continuous improvement.   
 Escalate systemic vendor-performance concerns to the HCM Vendor Operations Lead.   
 Identify recurring failure patterns and lead systemic technical improvements.   
 Enhancement & Small-to-Medium Project Delivery   
 Own Workday enhancements and small-to-medium projects that predominantly reside within the Workday domain.   
 Develop scope, estimates, resource plans, timelines, and delivery approaches.   
 Assign and coordinate appropriate functional, integration, security, testing, and AMS resources.   
 Manage execution through testing, deployment, stabilization, and operational transition.   
 Maintain accountability for the Workday components of larger cross-HCM programs led by Portfolio/Program Management.   
 Ensure project work does not unintentionally compromise PI or critical AMS commitments.   
 Workday Solution Management   
 Maintain strong knowledge of Workday functionality, configuration, integrations, security, and business-process dependencies within the assigned portfolio.   
 Develop strong relationships with HR and Payroll stakeholders and translate business priorities into sustainable Workday solutions.   
 Partner with the HCM Architect on changes involving significant architectural decisions.   
 Maximize standard Workday capabilities and reduce unnecessary customization.   
 Identify technical debt and include appropriate remediation in delivery planning.   
 Assess Workday release impacts and coordinate adoption of relevant new capabilities.   
 Balance immediate business requirements with long-term platform sustainability.   
 Production & Release Readiness   
 Ensure Workday changes follow established development, configuration, testing, security, migration, change, and production-control requirements.   
 Confirm appropriate technical and business testing has been completed and production-readiness criteria are met before deployment.   
 Validate production support, monitoring, deployment, rollback, and stabilization plans.   
 Engage the Technical Delivery Lead for complex, high-risk, or cross-platform releases.   
 Ensure post-production stabilization actions are completed and transitioned into normal operations.   
 Financial & Vendor Stewardship   
 Provide resource demand and capacity inputs into Workday forecasts and annual and ongoing capacity planning.   
 Monitor vendor capacity against funded commitments and planned demand; identify inefficient use of vendor capacity and recommend adjustments.   
 Validate that resource requests are backed by defined demand, outcomes, and appropriate skill requirements.   
 Partner with Vendor Operations on systemic provider-performance issues, contractual service expectations, and resource-model improvements.   
 Stakeholder & Delivery Governance   
 Serve as the primary HCM Technology delivery partner for the assigned Workday portfolio.   
 Give stakeholders clear visibility into commitments, capacity, delivery health, risks, and trade-offs.   
 Facilitate fact-based prioritization when demand exceeds capacity.   
 Resolve issues at the appropriate level, escalating decisions rather than routine execution problems.   
 Coordinate closely with other HCM Solution Managers where Workday work creates downstream dependencies.   
 Decision Rights   
 Although the role has no direct reports, the Workday Solutions Delivery Manager is empowered to:   
 Allocate Workday delivery resources across approved priorities and commitments.   
 Manage Workday delivery sequencing within established business priorities, and recommend sequencing changes when demand exceeds capacity.   
 Determine whether sufficient capacity and capability exist before accepting delivery commitments.   
 Hold AMS and delivery partners accountable for performance and resource quality, and require replacement or remediation plans for vendor resources that consistently do not meet expectations.   
 Make routine operational and delivery decisions without VP-level intervention.   
 Escalate cross-platform technical risks to the Technical Delivery Lead and architecture decisions to the HCM Architect.   
 Escalate material priority, funding, or business trade-offs with clear options and recommendations.   
 Basic Requirements   
 8+ years of progressive experience delivering Workday or comparable enterprise HCM solutions.   
 Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Human Resources, Business, Computer Science, or equivalent experience.   
 Demonstrated experience with Workday application delivery, enhancement management, AMS, and production support.   
 Proven experience managing resource capacity, allocation, and competing priorities across mixed internal and vendor delivery teams without direct reporting authority.   
 Experience leading PI Planning and managing multiple concurrent PI commitments, enhancements, production demands, and projects.   
 Strong working knowledge of Workday configuration, security, integrations, testing, and release management.   
 Strong understanding of incident, problem, change, release, and service-management disciplines.   
 Demonstrated ability to translate business demand into realistic resource and delivery plans.   
 Preferred Skills/Experience   
 Workday certifications and/or deep hands-on experience in the relevant Workday functional or technical domain (strongly preferred).   
 Experience managing global onshore/offshore delivery models and managed-service providers.   
 Experience with Agile delivery practices and ServiceNow-based service management.   
 Familiarity with SOX/ITGC, privacy, and audit requirements affecting HR technologies.   
 Strong vendor, stakeholder, and executive communication skills.   
 Ability to make decisions, manage trade-offs, and hold delivery teams and partners accountable for outcomes through influence.   
 Measures of Success   
 PI commitments delivered predictably with appropriate quality.   
 Resource capacity aligned to the highest-priority business outcomes.   
 Improved accuracy of resource forecasts and delivery commitments.   
 Capacity constraints and skill gaps identified before they affect delivery.   
 Reduced resource bottlenecks and dependence on individual SMEs.   
 Improved Workday platform stability, with fewer recurring incidents and a reduced AMS backlog.   
 Improved AMS resource capability, continuity, and accountability.   
 Small-to-medium initiatives delivered without unnecessary executive intervention.   
 Increased use of standard Workday capabilities and reduced avoidable technical debt.

ABOUT FLOAT

Float is on a mission to simplify finance for Canadian businesses, empowering them to eliminate complexity and unlock new opportunities. Through our innovative platform, Float enables businesses to streamline financial operations and optimize cash flow, so they can focus on what matters most: growth. 

 

As one of Canada’s fastest growing companies https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/rob-magazine/top-growing-companies/article-ranking-canadas-top-growing-companies-of-2024/ and top-rated startups in 2025 https://www.linkedin.com/posts/floatfinancial_were-proud-to-share-that-float-has-been-activity-7387093684720300032-2DDz/, 2024 https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/linkedin-top-startups-2024-15-canadian-companies-rise-linkedin-news-llihe/ and 2023 https://lnkd.in/TSU23CA, Float is customer-obsessed, passionate and entrepreneurial, with a team that includes leaders from Uber, Stripe, Shopify, Top Hat, Ada, Doordash, Snowflake, and Wealthsimple.

 

At Float, everyone is an owner, bringing their unique perspective to our team and product. Your voice is important, and we take having a culture based on feedback seriously. We openly share our thoughts and differing opinions so we can continue to improve. We do our best to keep our decision-making decentralized so that all team members feel ownership in our success.




OUR PRODUCT

Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C https://floatfinancial.com/press/float-financial-raises-cad-85-million-series-c, and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank.

 

Our team is a collection of ambitious, collaborative and mission-driven people from all walks of life but with one goal: helping Canadian companies not just survive but thrive. And we’re looking for bold innovators to help shape the future of business finance in Canada.




AI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS

We use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support parts of our hiring process. This may include AI-assisted scheduling and candidate communications, and AI-generated interview notes, guides or summaries to help our team focus on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Float is building an agent that works as a chief financial officer for every Canadian business: it knows the business, has all the context, and works around the clock. You would join the small team building the foundation for it, with a blank slate and a direct line to the product teams that will build on what you make.



You’ll have the best seat in the house on how to apply the frontier to real finance problems: taking raw model intelligence and turning it into durable, scalable, useful products. The team sits between the model providers, Float’s product teams, and the customers whose finances we run, building the harness —memory, skills, tools, evals, observability, distribution channels — that every agent at Float runs on.



This is a zero-to-one position. You will build the core pieces that let agents act reliably in production, and the interfaces and channels customers reach them through, then scale them across Float’s products. The field is moving quickly, so the best people here learn fast and are glad to rebuild something when a better approach arrives.



We are hiring across multiple levels for this role. Our interview process evaluates scope, judgment and learning velocity, and we level accordingly. At Staff, you set the patterns the harness is built on and the evaluation and observability bar every agent at Float meets. This role suits engineers who have shipped agents to real users, want more ownership than a large company can offer, and like to build.




WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Ship agents that save customers real money and time. Take them from the first prototype to production at scale, and own the outcome once they’re live.

 - Build the unified harness. Context management, capabilities and tool use, evaluation, monitoring and observability — the layer every agent at Float runs on and scales through.

 - Make agent actions safe to trust with a company’s money. Permissions, approvals, audit trails, and clear behaviour when the agent is uncertain or wrong.

 - Define what good looks like and measure it. Offline evals, production monitoring of agent decisions, and the loop that turns incidents into improvements.

 - Build the interfaces agents are delivered through. Chat, generative UI, and multiple channels at once.

 - Make product teams faster. Partner with them so they can launch their own agent capabilities on the harness without rebuilding it.

 - Stay on the frontier. Track models, inference and context management, and rework what we’ve built when a better approach appears.

 - Representative projects:
   
   - Build the approval and audit layer that lets an agent pay a bill on a customer’s behalf.
   
   - Stand up the evaluation framework that tells us, before and after launch, whether an agent’s answers about a company’s spend are correct.
   
   - Give agents the context of a whole business — cards, bills, accounts, accounting integrations — in a form that stays accurate and token-efficient.
   
   - Ship the tooling that enables a product team to launch agentic capabilities without our help.




ABOUT YOU


HERE'S WHAT SETS YOU UP FOR SUCCESS AT FLOAT:

 - You Put Customers First, Always. You care deeply about delivering meaningful value. Whether you're building internal systems or customer-facing features, you're always thinking about how to make life better for our users.

 - You Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, step up to challenges, and seek solutions proactively—doing what's best for the business, not just your role.

 - You Think Big and Move Fast. You're energized by building from 0 to 1. You're not afraid to challenge the status quo, experiment quickly, and learn as you go.

 - You Constantly Learn and Grow. You're hungry to improve your craft and open to feedback. You bring a growth mindset to everything you do.

 - You Raise the Bar. You care about doing things well and efficiently. You balance speed with rigor and always look for ways to improve how we work.

 - You Win as a Team. You're a generous collaborator who values communication, context, and shared wins. You lift others up and help make the team stronger.


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE:

 - Experience building and shipping agents or LLM-backed systems to production, and running them there: monitoring, improving and scaling them. Typically 5+ years of software engineering for Senior, 8+ for Staff, with a track record of technical leadership across teams at Staff.

 - Depth in one of two areas: full-stack product engineering for agentic experiences, or backend engineering for LLM pipelines and agent infrastructure.

 - Hands-on, current knowledge of frontier models, inference and context management, and opinions about what works.

 - Comfort giving agents capabilities and context and then observing them, rather than specifying every step.

 - Experience at more than one company stage, or in a company growing quickly, with major ownership and impact.

 - A habit of building things nobody asked you for, and finishing them.

 - Curiosity, and the willingness to start over when the field moves.


STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO HAVE:

 - Experience as a founder, founding engineer, or early engineer on a major initiative inside a larger company.

 - Experience building systems that move money or make decisions people are accountable for — fintech, payments, or other regulated products.

 - Experience designing evaluation frameworks for LLM systems, including LLM-as-judge and human-in-the-loop labelling.


THIS MAY NOT BE THE ROLE FOR YOU IF: 

 - You prefer a defined roadmap and a fully specified process.

 - You have spent your whole career in a large company and want similar scope here.

 - You are attached to approaches you have already built and would rather defend them than replace them.

 - You are looking for a role where AI is a side tool rather than the core of the work.




OUR HIRING PHILOSOPHY

We hire for character, curiosity, and learning velocity before credentials. Titles matter less than impact, and every hire is expected to raise the bar for Float as a whole.




WHY YOU SHOULD JOIN

IN SHORT

ELYSIS-Stagiaire Industrialisation d’équipement de production - (Hiver 2027)
 Une nouvelle ère pour l’industrie de l’aluminium – ELYSIS 
 Aluminium sans carbone 
 La technologie ELYSIS™ représente la plus grande avancée dans l’industrie de l’aluminium depuis 1886. Des efforts sont présentement déployés afin de perfectionner cette nouvelle façon révolutionnaire de produire de l’aluminium, qui élimine le dioxyde de carbone et toutes les autres émissions de gaz à effet de serre du procédé conventionnel d’électrolyse.
 Le procédé ELYSIS élimine l’utilisation d’anodes de carbone, en les remplaçant par des matériaux brevetés. En tant que premier procédé industriel qui émet de l’oxygène comme sous-produit, il a le potentiel de transformer toute l’industrie.
 En 2018, deux producteurs d’aluminium de calibre international, Alcoa et Rio Tinto, ont uni leurs forces afin de créer la coentreprise ELYSIS avec le gouvernement du Québec. Bénéficiant du soutien du gouvernement du Canada et d’Apple, la technologie progresse et elle est actuellement conçue pour être utilisée aussi bien dans des projets de construction que de modernisation d’alumineries. 
 ELYSIS a son siège social à Montréal, avec des centres de recherche et de développement à Alma et à Jonquière, au Québec (Canada), ainsi qu’à New Kensington, en Pennsylvanie (États-Unis) et en France.
 Du métal de qualité commerciale produit par ELYSIS dans nos installations R&D et au centre de développement industriel est déjà utilisé par Apple dans un éventail de produits (comme le MacBook Pro 16 po et l’iPhone SE), par AB InBev (canettes) et par Audi (roues du e-tron GT, fabriqués par le RONAL Group).

Il vous permettra également de vous immerger dans un environnement à forte teneur R&D et de vous faire comprendre l’importance de la protection de l’information.

Executive Operations (Exec Ops) Chief of Staff Track, 12–18 Months) 
 If you’re a highly organized, extremely self-accountable, love project management (think Trello/Asana), and desire to grow into the 2nd in command of a fast growing startup… then this might just be your dream job. 
 My name is Richard Yu, I’m the founder/CEO of a fast-growing education + software business. 
 Across all social, my media team and I have built a 1.5M+ follower platform (@richardyuzee on IG, as an example).
 My #1 responsibility is to spend 40 hours/week being the talent (face of our content), and visionary (having long blocks of 4 hrs/day) where I can think about vision and growth strategies.
 That means I need to spend all my time creating content, driving strategy, and making high-leverage decisions… and this is where you come in.
 Your job is to protect my time, eliminate operational drag, and make sure the company actually executes.
 This role is Exec Ops / Office of the CEO — think of it as a supercharged Executive Assistant with a real path to Chief of Staff, based on performance. You will be my execution arm and second brain, with high trust, high access, and high expectations.
 This is not a “cute admin” job. It’s also not a glamorous strategy-only job. It’s the real work: calendar, follow-ups, accountability, systems, project management, hiring ops, and getting things done
 What you’ll own (your responsibilities)
 1) CEO Time + Calendar (your #1 responsibility)
 Own my calendar ruthlessly: protect deep work blocks, batch meetings, enforce priorities
 Gate time, not people (you’re not allowed to be a “gatekeeper” personality)
 Turn chaos into an intentional weekly schedule that matches company goals
 2) Internal Communication + Follow-Up
 Run the follow-up engine: action items, owners, due dates, reminders, escalation
 Ensure nothing dies in Slack/WhatsApp/email because people “got busy”
 Draft messages/emails and internal updates so I can approve quickly
 3) Project Management + Accountability (across the whole org)
 Build/quarterback the company operating system (Trello/Asana/Notion—whatever we standardize)
 Every project has: owner, deadline, next action, definition of done
 Hold leaders accountable (ex: Moe accountable to deliverables, Bashar accountable to reporting cadence, content team accountable to output)
 4) Hiring Operations (big focus right now)
 Run end-to-end hiring ops for key roles: Organic Content Director, Senior DR Copywriter/Head of Marketing, IG Copywriter, etc.
 Manage pipeline, scheduling, scorecards, assignments, Loom reviews, references
 Keep the process moving fast without me getting dragged into logistics
 5) Content Operations Oversight (not creating content)
 Ensure content machines ship on time: YouTube, IG, email—whatever is on the calendar gets done on time. 
 Track weekly output + deadlines + approvals so I’m not chasing people 
 You must be insanely detail oriented and VERY good at calling people out and holding them accountable. 
 6) Metrics + Reporting
 Monthly P&L request/collection, KPI dashboards, and weekly reporting rhythm
 You will analyze the Profit & Loss statement every month, analyze the payroll (yes you will know how much everyone gets paid), and provide extremely detailed recommendations on who should get raises, comp structure adjustments, who is being inefficient, who needs to get cut, etc. 
 7) Personal + Local Projects (as needed)
 Help execute real-life projects that support business performance (ex: managing the build-out of a home studio in Puerto Rico)
 Spanish is preferred because it helps with local execution, but it’s not required. If you’re insanely quick with a translator / ChatGPT for messages, works as well. 
 8) AI Emphasis 
 You should come with batteries included with understanding how to use AI in your workflow. The most BASIC version of this is ChatGPT instead of using Google, that’s the bare bare minimum. 
 You should be so good with AI that you are now giving feedback and suggestions to OTHER department leaders on how they should be using AI in their day to day responsiblities. 
 What success looks like (KPIs)
 20+ hours/week of my time returned within 60–90 days
 I stop doing: project management, follow-ups, DM appointment setting, internal chasing, hiring logistics
 Weekly operating rhythm runs without me pushing it
 Projects move faster, less stress, fewer dropped balls
 The company becomes calmer and more accountable — not more chaotic
 Who this is for
 This is for you if:
 You’re an operator: you love execution, structure, and turning chaos into order
 You have extreme ownership: you don’t wait to be told, you anticipate
 You can make good decisions without asking me every day for permission.
 You’re comfortable being in the background while I’m front-facing in the content
 You’re discreet and trustworthy (you will see everything)
 You’re strong at writing and communication (VERY detailed reports, clear, direct)
 You enjoy running a tight system and holding people accountable
 Who this is NOT for
 This is not for you if:
 You want a “strategy-only” role where you get to “bounce ideas” with Richard without doing admin, follow-ups, or nitty-gritty execution
 You need constant direction, reassurance, or step-by-step instructions where you get “coaching” from Richard (FYI - you’re here to protect my time, not get “free mentorship” from Richard).
 You avoid conflict and can’t hold people accountable in tough conversations when they’re late or underperforming 
 You’re not comfortable with high access + high confidentiality
 You get offended by doing “unsexy” tasks — this role includes them. 
 Example: 3-4 hour project of looking at every single expense item on Richard’s AMEX credit card statement to identify for software and expenses that we are overpaying on, and then reaching out to each software company to cancel them. 
 You should be smart to DO IT ONCE, and either build a system to automate this, delegate to someone else, or you just own this ongoing monthly moving forward. 
 The truth: the trade-off (good, bad, and ugly)
 You will get full context: you’ll see my schedule, meetings, priorities, and how decisions get made in real time. This is high-speed CEO training.

 coordinating hiring logistics and keeping candidates moving along by messaging them on iMessage and Whatsapp on my behalf

 You act as my internal execution arm while I focus on content + strategy

Role Overview

 Employment Type: Full-time, permanent
 Openings: 2
 Target Start Date: January 2027
 About elia 
 elia is the all-in-one workplace operations platform for large organizations. Desk and room booking, visitor management, occupancy sensors, smart lockers, digital signage, asset management: we bring it all together in a single platform. Large organizations trust us in Canada, the United States, and around the world. We are a fast-growing team of about 40 people, and we plan to reach about 120 over the next three years. Everyone has a direct impact on the product and on how we build the company, and AI is part of how we work.
 The Role 
 Ask anyone who runs an office for a large company what their week looks like: meeting rooms double-booked, desks empty on Friday and fought over on Wednesday, visitors waiting at reception because nobody knew they were coming, and five different tools that don't talk to each other.
 elia fixes that with one platform for the teams who run the workplace: Facilities, IT, and HR. We work with large organizations across Canada, and we are building our sales team in Toronto.
 As an SDR, you open the door. You call people in Ontario's largest organizations, start real conversations about how their workplace runs, and book the discovery calls our Account Executive turns into deals. This is a high-volume phone role: you spend your days calling people you have never met.
 What You Will Do 
 Make a high volume of cold calls every day to a defined list of large Ontario organizations (500+ employees).
 Use the phone as your main channel, supported by email and LinkedIn.
 Research each account before you reach out, so every call has a real reason behind it.
 Book discovery calls with the right people in Facilities, Workplace, Real Estate, IT, and HR.
 Write a clear handoff note for every call: who is attending, what problem they likely have, and why now.
 Make sure prospects show up, and rebook when they don't.
 Work closely with your Account Executive on which accounts to go after each month.
 Keep HubSpot accurate ("If it isn't in the CRM, it didn't happen").
 What You Bring 
 Ideally some experience calling prospects or customers cold: an outbound or SDR role, telemarketing, recruiting, or inside sales (any industry works; you do not need to know ours).
 Recent graduates with real motivation for a sales career are welcome (experience gives you an edge, drive gets you in the door).
 Comfort on the phone all day: you call people and don't hide behind email.
 Resilience: most calls get no answer, and you keep going anyway.
 Curiosity about how businesses work, and the discipline to research before you reach out.
 Clear spoken and written English.
 A quiet home workspace where you can make calls all day.
 French is an asset.
 Comfortable with Technologies 
 You should be comfortable with technologies and already be leveraging AI tools in your day-to-day work.
 We are looking for someone who is tech-savvy, understands platforms well, and is curious to try out different tools.
 Where This Role Leads 
 This is the first step on a published sales career ladder, not a dead end. The path is defined by a formula, not by opinion: SDRs move through five levels with clear targets, then to Sales Associate, where you own and close your own deals, and then to Account Executive. Strong performers are promoted to Sales Associate, often within about a year. You learn the workplace market from the ground up, and that knowledge is what moves you up.
 What We Offer 
 Uncapped commission, based on the discovery calls you generate that our team then completes.
 A clear, published career ladder from SDR to Sales Associate to Account Executive.
 A home office we equip for you (as there is no Toronto office for now; a shared workspace may come later).
 A flexible schedule.
 Free access to Tonic Gym, or $100 toward sports.
 Our famous G-PHEST team events.
 Comprehensive group insurance.

 As a Senior Accounts Receivable Associate, you will support the Invoice to Cash (I2C) team by serving as the research and resolution engine behind the Collections and Cash Application teams. You will own the JIRA queue end to end, conduct account reconciliations, coordinate with internal teams to investigate and resolve inquiries, and provide findings that are either fully resolved or ready for the collector to communicate to the customer.

 Au cours de vos 90 premiers jours de travail…

ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.



THE ROLE

The Model Performance organization at Baseten is looking to hire our first Technical Program Manager. This is a zero-to-one role in a team that is responsible for building the core algorithms and methods that power Baseten’s high performance inference stack. You won't inherit an existing program framework, you'll build one from the ground up: the planning structure, execution processes, metrics and the cross-functional alignment that a fast-growing organization needs. Your contributions will directly impact how fast our performance R&D gets productized. If you can drive turning a set of ambitious but loosely defined initiatives into a predictable, well-governed program, this role is for you.

EXAMPLE INITIATIVES

Take a look at these blog posts written by members of our Model Performance team:

 - How to build a day-0 API for Kimi K3 https://www.baseten.co/blog/how-to-build-a-day-zero-api-for-kimi-k3/

 - How we built the new fastest API for GLM-5.2 https://www.baseten.co/blog/how-we-built-the-new-fastest-api-for-glm-52/

 - Inference engineering for DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 https://www.baseten.co/blog/inference-engineering-for-deepseek-v4-pro-0813/

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own execution across Model Performance's active project portfolio, freeing the team's technical leads to focus on technical direction rather than tracking.

 - Design and stand up the planning structures, operating cadences, and status reporting mechanisms that best fits the team’s DNA.

 - Coordinate model release and optimization programs end to end, including day-zero launches, sequencing the work across performance engineering, infra, and release stakeholders.

 - Drive cross-team alignment as scope expands from Model Performance Core into Model APIs and the inference production stack (BIS).

 - Surface risks and dependencies early, and keep leadership informed with clear, honest status.

 - Partner with engineering leads to design team structures and ownership boundaries as the org scales.

REQUIREMENTS

 - Deep technical program management experience - you're already running programs of this scope at an organization of similar or greater complexity.

 - Experience program-managing model performance or inference optimization work - you understand how engines like vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang, or NVIDIA Dynamo fit into a production serving stack and can engage credibly with the engineers building on them.

 - Demonstrated comfort with ambiguity and zero-to-one program building, not just executing an existing framework.

 - Proven ability to influence without authority across engineers, managers, and leadership who don't report to you.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to make deeply technical programs legible to any audience.

 - High agency decision making that demonstrates ownership, accountability and a strong desire to get things done.

ABOUT VALSOFT VENTURES 
 Valsoft is a Montreal-based company that acquires and grows vertical market software businesses, with a portfolio of 140+ companies that spans dozens of industries and countries. Valsoft Ventures is where we build new companies from scratch. Each venture starts with a founder in residence and runs on Valsoft’s capital, infrastructure, and support, and its first customers often come from inside Valsoft’s own portfolio.
 THE OPPORTUNITY 
 We’re looking for a Tax Manager to own tax for the companies Ventures builds (currently 4). You’ll set each new company up correctly from the start, keep it compliant as it grows, and build the process every future venture follows. The work centres on Canada and the U.S., with filings elsewhere coordinated through local advisors as ventures enter new markets.
 In one week you might register a new entity, review a U.S. state return for an older venture, and walk a founder in residence through what QST means for their first Quebec customer. The hard part is that every venture is different and none of them waits for tax. Founders move fast, priorities shift when a venture changes direction, and you’ll often set up a company whose product isn’t finished yet.
 AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research, draft, analyze, and automate. You’re responsible for the quality of the result.
 WHAT YOU’LL DO 
 Set up each new venture correctly. When Ventures decides to build a company, you’ll work out what tax needs to be in place before it takes its first customer: structuring input, registrations, elections, and how its products and pricing are taxed. You’ll work with the founder in residence, Valsoft’s finance and legal teams, and the VP, Tax on structuring decisions.
 Run compliance across the ventures. Manage Canadian federal and provincial corporate income tax returns and U.S. federal and state income and franchise tax returns for each venture, reviewing what external providers prepare. Keep a tax calendar, records, and audit files for every company, and resolve notices and correspondence from the CRA, Revenu Québec, the IRS, and state authorities.
 Own sales and indirect tax. Own U.S. sales and use tax for the ventures: nexus monitoring, registrations, taxability analysis, filing, and remittance. In Canada, manage GST/HST and QST, including registrations, returns, and input tax credit and input tax refund recovery.
 Handle intercompany and group reporting. Ventures run on Valsoft’s capital, infrastructure, and support, which means intercompany arrangements from the first day. Set up and document those arrangements, coordinate transfer pricing documentation with external advisors in line with CRA, IRS, and OECD guidelines, and support any inquiries.
 Build the tax process Ventures runs on. Design the processes, controls, and tools that let tax keep up as the number of ventures grows, and decide where a tax engine or automation is worth adding. Founders, finance, and legal will treat you as their main contact on tax, and you’ll explain requirements in plain terms.
 WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR 
 A CPA designation (Canada or U.S.) and at least 4 years of post-designation tax experience in public accounting or a corporate tax environment, with exposure to both Canadian and U.S. tax.
 Working knowledge of transfer pricing, international tax, and tax accounting under IFRS.
 You can look at a new business model and work out what tax it triggers before it launches, and give a founder a clear answer they can act on the same day.
 You prepare, review, and file returns yourself, and you manage external advisors and hold them to deadlines and quality.
 You use AI to research, draft, and analyze, and you check the output before it goes anywhere.

 USEFUL EXPERIENCE

 À PROPOS DE VALSOFT VENTURES 
 Valsoft est une entreprise montréalaise qui acquiert et fait croître des entreprises de logiciels de marchés verticaux, avec un portefeuille de plus de 140 entreprises couvrant des dizaines de secteurs d’activité et de pays.. Valsoft Ventures, c’est là où nous bâtissons de nouvelles entreprises à partir de zéro. Chacune démarre avec un fondateur en résidence et s’appuie sur le capital, l’infrastructure et le soutien de Valsoft, et ses premiers clients proviennent souvent du portefeuille même de Valsoft.
 LE DÉFI 
 Nous cherchons une ou un gestionnaire, fiscalité pour prendre en charge la fiscalité des entreprises que bâtit Ventures (actuellement 4). Vous mettrez chaque nouvelle entreprise sur les bons rails dès le départ, veillerez à sa conformité à mesure qu’elle grandit et bâtirez le processus que suivra chaque entreprise future. Le travail porte principalement sur le Canada et les États-Unis ; ailleurs, les déclarations sont coordonnées avec des conseillers locaux à mesure que les entreprises entrent dans de nouveaux marchés.
 En une semaine, vous pourriez immatriculer une nouvelle entité, réviser la déclaration d’un État américain pour une entreprise plus établie et expliquer à un fondateur en résidence ce que la TVQ signifie pour son premier client québécois. La difficulté, c’est que chaque entreprise est différente et qu’aucune n’attend que la fiscalité soit prête. Les fondateurs avancent vite, les priorités changent quand une entreprise change de cap, et vous mettrez souvent sur pied une entreprise dont le produit n’est pas encore terminé.
 L’IA devrait faire partie de votre façon de travailler. Utilisez-la pour faire de la recherche, rédiger, analyser et automatiser. La qualité du résultat demeure votre responsabilité.

 Bien démarrer chaque nouvelle entreprise. Lorsque Ventures décide de bâtir une entreprise, vous déterminerez ce qui doit être en place sur le plan fiscal avant qu’elle serve son premier client : conseils sur la structure, inscriptions, choix fiscaux et traitement fiscal de ses produits et de sa tarification. Vous travaillerez avec le fondateur en résidence, les équipes des finances et des affaires juridiques de Valsoft, ainsi qu’avec le VP, Fiscalité sur les décisions de structuration.
 Assurer la conformité de l’ensemble des entreprises. Gérer les déclarations de revenus fédérales et provinciales des sociétés au Canada, ainsi que les déclarations de revenus fédérales et d’État et les déclarations de taxe de franchise aux États-Unis pour chaque entreprise, en révisant le travail préparé par les fournisseurs externes. Tenir un calendrier fiscal, des registres et des dossiers de vérification pour chaque société, et régler les avis et la correspondance de l’ARC, de Revenu Québec, de l’IRS et des autorités des États.
 Prendre en charge la taxe de vente et les taxes indirectes. Gérer la taxe de vente et d’utilisation américaine pour les entreprises : suivi du lien fiscal (nexus), inscriptions, analyse de l’assujettissement, production des déclarations et versements. Au Canada, gérer la TPS/TVH et la TVQ, y compris les inscriptions, les déclarations et la récupération des crédits de taxe sur les intrants (CTI) et des remboursements de la taxe sur les intrants (RTI).
 Gérer les ententes intersociétés et les rapports du groupe. Les entreprises de Ventures reposent sur le capital, l’infrastructure et le soutien de Valsoft, ce qui implique des ententes intersociétés dès le premier jour. Mettre en place et documenter ces ententes, coordonner la documentation sur les prix de transfert avec des conseillers externes conformément aux lignes directrices de l’ARC, de l’IRS et de l’OCDE, et répondre à toute demande de renseignements.
 Bâtir le processus fiscal de Ventures. Concevoir les processus, les contrôles et les outils qui permettront à la fiscalité de suivre le rythme à mesure que le nombre d’entreprises augmente, et déterminer où un moteur de calcul fiscal ou l’automatisation en vaut la peine.  CE QUE NOUS RECHERCHONS 
 Un titre de CPA (Canada ou États-Unis) et au moins 4 ans d’expérience en fiscalité après l’obtention du titre, en cabinet comptable ou en entreprise, touchant à la fois la fiscalité canadienne et américaine.
 Une connaissance pratique des prix de transfert, de la fiscalité internationale et de la comptabilisation des impôts selon les IFRS.
 Vous savez analyser un nouveau modèle d’affaires et en déterminer les incidences fiscales avant son lancement, puis donner à un fondateur une réponse claire sur laquelle il peut agir le jour même.
 Vous préparez, révisez et produisez vous-même des déclarations, et vous gérez des conseillers externes en exigeant le respect des échéances et de la qualité.
 Vous utilisez l’IA pour faire de la recherche, rédiger et analyser, et vous vérifiez le résultat avant qu’il aille plus loin.
 Vous travaillez de façon autonome, faites avancer les calendriers de plusieurs sociétés en même temps, terminez ce que vous commencez et tenez des dossiers qu’un vérificateur peut suivre.
 EXPÉRIENCE UTILE 
 Conformité pratique en matière de taxe de vente et d’utilisation américaine, ainsi que de TPS/TVH et de TVQ
 Fiscalité des entreprises en démarrage ou nouvellement constituées, y compris le traitement des logiciels et du SaaS en matière de taxe de vente
 Divulgations volontaires
 Expérience au sein d’un groupe comptant de nombreuses filiales
 CE QUE NOUS VALORISONS 
 Un jugement sûr et le souci du détail.
 Le sens des responsabilités et la capacité de terminer le travail sans avoir besoin de relances.
 La compréhension de la façon dont une jeune entreprise génère des revenus et de la façon dont la fiscalité en découle.
 La curiosité et la volonté de changer une approche qui ne fonctionne pas.
 L’honnêteté de dire quand une position n’est pas défendable, y compris la vôtre.
 À QUOI RESSEMBLE LA RÉUSSITE 
 Au cours de vos six premiers mois, chaque entreprise existante dispose d’un calendrier fiscal à jour, des inscriptions nécessaires, d’une analyse du lien fiscal en matière de taxe de vente et d’un dossier de vérification que quelqu’un d’autre pourrait reprendre.
 La prochaine entreprise lancée par Ventures passe par votre liste de vérification de démarrage et applique la bonne taxe dès sa première facture.
 Les ententes intersociétés sont documentées, et l’équipe fiscale centrale de Valsoft reçoit de votre part, dans les délais, les données sur les impôts et les rapports du groupe.
 D’ici la fin de votre première année, les fondateurs vous consultent avant de modifier leur tarification ou d’entrer dans un nouveau marché, et non après. Un fondateur mentionne un nouveau modèle de tarification le lundi ; le mercredi, vous avez déterminé où il crée un lien fiscal et ce que la facture doit indiquer.

Who we are

 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. 
 About the team 
 The Link Partnerships team sources, develops, and manages relationships with the payments ecosystem partners that power Link, Stripe's consumer wallet. Our team drives the growth and utility of Link by building partnerships with card networks, card issuers, local payment methods, crypto providers, and emerging commerce platforms. We execute on high-impact, cross-functional initiatives that expand Link's acceptance, improve performance, and enable new payment experiences—including agentic commerce. These partnerships have a significant impact on Stripe and the products used by millions of our users.
 What you’ll do 
 We're looking for a Partner Development Manager who builds and manages Link's payments partnerships with card networks, card issuers, local payment method providers, and crypto and stablecoin providers. You'll own the strategy and execution of partnerships that expand Link's payment capabilities, improve transaction performance, and position Link as the default payments layer for agentic commerce. You'll negotiate commercial agreements, drive technical integrations, and shape Link's payments roadmap in collaboration with these partners. As part of these efforts, you'll collaborate closely with cross-functional stakeholders, including Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, Risk, and others. You'll also lead relationship management and partner closely with external partners' executive leadership.

 Define and execute Link's payments partnership strategy across card networks, card issuers, local payment methods, and crypto and stablecoins
 Negotiate and manage commercial agreements with payment partners that expand Link's acceptance footprint, improve authorization rates, and unlock new payment capabilities
 Develop a deep understanding of the card network and issuer landscape—including scheme rules, tokenization frameworks, authentication protocols, and competitive dynamics—to inform partnership strategy
 Drive partnerships that enable Link to serve as the payments layer for agentic commerce, working with networks and issuers to establish rules, liability frameworks, and technical standards for agent-initiated transactions
 Gather inputs from and coordinate with internal cross-functional stakeholders (including product, risk, compliance, engineering, and security) to drive creation and execution of partner strategy including our global LPM roadmap
 Work closely with Product and Engineering to define requirements and shape Link's payments product roadmap based on partner capabilities and market opportunities
 Identify partner stakeholders who will champion Stripe, educate them about Link's value proposition, and build alignment between Stripe and our partners' executive teams
 Identify and effectively analyze new partnership opportunities, ultimately making recommendations to relevant decision makers and cross-functional stakeholders

 You're a skilled dealmaker and a strategist by nature. You understand how to work closely with Product and Engineering teams and can formulate partner strategies that drive tangible and measurable results. You're energized by the intersection of payments infrastructure and emerging commerce models, and you see the opportunity to define how payments work in an agentic world.

 10+ years of experience in partnerships, business development, corporate development, or related field
 5+ years of experience in or working closely with card networks, card issuers, digital wallets, or payments infrastructure providers
 3+ years of experience negotiating commercial deals with partners, including scaling such deals across multiple partners
 Strong communication skills, in both verbal and written form, and ability to influence stakeholders across a wide variety of functions, including at executive levels
 Technical acumen, especially an ability to understand product strategy and use this understanding to define requirements for scaling products through partnerships

 Strong agency, can handle ambiguity in a fast-moving organization, and thrives on a high level of autonomy and responsibility

Rockstar is recruiting for a leading organization dedicated to advancing decentralized finance (DeFi) through innovative protocol engineering and product design. The client is a mission-driven foundation supporting the growth, decentralization, and sustainability of the Uniswap ecosystem, with a focus on driving value across protocol innovation, developer support, governance, research, and security. This role offers the opportunity to work at the forefront of DeFi, collaborating with a team committed to building impactful, open financial infrastructure.
 v4 Hooks Architect 
 A senior builder is sought who operates at the intersection of protocol engineering and DeFi product design. This individual will design, prototype, and productionize Uniswap v4 hooks that unlock new markets. Areas of focus include dynamic fee markets, JIT‑aware liquidity protections, programmable compliance for RWAs, solver/intents integrations, perps/credit primitives, and beyond.
 Why this role exists 
 - Hooks are the frontier. Uniswap v4 turns AMM behavior into a programmable surface. The ecosystem needs more production-ready hooks to go from tinkering to real usage.
 - Builders need partners. High‑quality hooks require deep protocol knowledge and product instincts designing the onchain mechanics, the incentives, and a path to distribution.
 - The mandate: accelerate onchain trading activity and protocol support across Uniswap deployments. This role is central to that impact.
 The work 
 - Bring product thinking for market‑tailored hooks: Ideate/incubate high‑leverage ideas across market segments: volatile pairs (ETH/USDx, xBTC/USDx), correlated/stable pairs (USDx–USDx), and order sizes from small retail to whales. Translate these insights into concrete hook specs with clear adoption and measurement plans.
 - Architect & ship hooks: Own the full lifecycle from whiteboard to an audited mainnet deployment that advances the roadmap (fee dynamics, liquidity management, MEV/LVR capture, KYC/attestations, JIT, etc.).
 - Author canonical patterns: Publish reference implementations, hook templates, and “living specs” that other teams can safely extend.
 - Design with distribution in mind: Co‑create adoption plans with other DeFi protocols (lending/ALMs/vaults), aggregators/routers, intent layers, asset issuers. Ship the adapters, simulators, and SDK glue to make integration easy.
 - Own security & correctness: Threat model hooks, define invariants, fuzz and formally verify critical paths, and partner with external auditors.
 - Data & feedback loops: Work with the data team to instrument events/metrics, write Dune/Flipside dashboards, and run controlled experiments to tune parameters (fees, tick ranges, JIT thresholds) based on observed flow, MEV, and LP PnL.
 A week in this role might look like 
 - Ideate, architect, and implement a new stable‑stable hook designed to win $100k+ trades (market‑share target, slippage/fee behavior, routing incentives, aggregator integration plan).
 - Design abstractions for reusability and code hygiene. Upstream libraries into a canonical toolkit.
 - Pair programming and code reviews with an external team on a lending rehypothecation hook design and implementation.
 - Write Foundry tests and fuzzers for beforeSwap/afterSwap invariants; benchmark gas and optimize with Yul where it pays.
 - Coordinate with an aggregator on simulation support and revert reasons; land a PR to their router.
 What success looks like 
 3 months
 - Land one high‑leverage hook in audit or on testnet with credible distribution partners.
 - Establish a metrics schema and dashboard framework for hook evaluation (LP PnL, orderflow capture, effective liquidity).
 6 months
 - Two production hooks with measurable flow/TVL and zero critical incidents.
 - Clear adoption playbooks for routers, wallets, and solver layers; at least three third‑party teams shipping on these patterns.
 - Demonstrated LP or trader outcome improvements.
 - Moved the needle on core KPIs.
 Minimum qualifications 
 - 3+ years smart‑contract engineering, with 2+ years shipping production DeFi at protocol teams (DEX, lending, perps, bridges, market making infrastructure, oracles).
 - Deep Solidity and EVM internals; strong with Foundry, fuzzing, property tests; comfort reading/implementing community smart contracts.
 - Knowledge of the most common security pitfalls.
 - Deep and practical understanding of Uniswap v4 architecture (PoolManager, Hooks, singleton design, state scoping, callback surfaces).
 - Practical understanding of Uniswap v3 concentrated liquidity model.
 - Strong understanding of liquidity routing infrastructure - aggregators, routers, and solvers.
 - Demonstrated product sense in DeFi: able to reason about incentives, MEV, LP/trader UX, and distribution realities.
 - A portfolio of shipped, battle‑tested contracts and public design docs, posts, or talks.
 Nice‑to‑have signals 
 - Shipped a v4 hook on mainnet with end‑to‑end readiness - hands‑on learnings and production experience are desirable.
 - Emphasis on scalable and organized testing suites. Test-driven design practices.
 How the team works 
 - Product focused: Intentional about building for target markets instead of randomly throwing ideas. There is no one DEX design that fits all use cases, so markets are approached with different lenses - Ethereum volatile pairs, stable‑stable pairs, BTC‑fi pairs, RWAs and also chain dynamics (Arbitrum vs Base vs Mainnet vs Unichain).
 - Velocity with security as a feature: Focused on solving one problem at a time and shipping with high velocity, without compromising on security. Staged rollouts, clear escape hatches, no heroics.
 - Small, senior squads: Initiatives are led, not tickets.
 - Data‑anchored decisions: ship → measure → iterate.
 - Public goods stewardship: Like Ethereum core devs, the team acts as stewards of shared infrastructure. Primitives are designed with ecosystem adoption in mind, ensuring they are neutral, composable, and useful beyond just one chain.
 Application prompts (short and telling) 
 Please include two things with the application:
 1. A hook idea to ship in the next 12 weeks. Explain why and how this idea would be chosen: how the market opportunity is mapped, the target pair defined, trade segment, and reasoning through ecosystem router/aggregator integration.
    - Outline: state, which lifecycle callbacks would be used (beforeInitialize/beforeSwap/afterSwap/…), key invariants, and gas/MEV risks.
 2. A link to a deployed DeFi contract & Github from a previous project that facilitates valuable economic activity. What was the initial design, and how did it evolve as market‑share dynamics were observed?
    - While not all developers write multi-million dollar TVL contracts, DeFi insight, security, and learnings along the way are especially valued.
 Interview flow (what to expect) 
 - 30‑min intro: mandate & portfolio walkthrough.
 - Deep‑dive design exercise: scope a hook and discuss edge cases, tests, and rollout plan.
 - Live code review: read a small v4 hook and identify risks; write 2–3 properties to fuzz.
 - Security focused interview with Security collaborator.
 - Product/strategy chat with Growth: adoption plan, partners, and metrics.
 - Take home assignment: implement a hook involving flash accounting and provide a robust test suite.

 In pursuit of a more open and fair financial system, the client supports the growth, decentralization, and sustainability of the Uniswap community. Through grants, value is driven in five key focus areas: Protocol and Innovation, Developers, Governance, Research, and Security. The grant making approach is designed to maximize positive impact, bringing in new contributors to the community who focus on building new initiatives, committees, products, infrastructure, and more.
